segments.text: 同学们好。今天讲二零二六年新课标一卷的读后续写，第六十七题，满分二十五分。
题目要求：根据材料内容和所给的两段开头语，续写两段，词数一百五十个左右。‖我们的范文，每段八十八个词，合计一百七十六个词。
第一段开头：丹尼尔和瑞秋建议艾米丽坐火车，继续她的旅程。
第二段开头：三天后，艾米丽回来取她的车。
先看满分要求。评分标准第五档，二十一到二十五分，有四条。
第一，与原文内容融洽，和两段开头语衔接合理。
segments.note: ① 与原文融洽，与开头语衔接合理

segments.text: 第二，内容丰富。
segments.note: ② 内容丰富

segments.text: 第三，语法结构和词汇丰富、准确。
segments.note: ③ 语法结构和词汇丰富、准确

segments.text: 第四，有效使用语句间的连接成分，结构紧凑。‖后面每一句的得分点，都会落到这四条上。
segments.note: ④ 有效使用连接成分，结构紧凑

segments.text: 先读原文。第一段交代人物和目的：艾米丽，二十五岁，十二月二十三日出发，要赶到多伦多，和男朋友一起过圣诞。‖这是全文的目标，续写要给出结果。
mark: Emily Sanders, a 25-year-old from Detroit, Michigan
reaching Toronto to meet her boyfriend for Christmas
segments.note: 人物与目标：赶去多伦多，和男朋友过圣诞

segments.text: 冲突从哪里来？‖她听到了暴风雪预警，却没放在心上；雪越下越大，她被引下高速，开上一条陌生的路。
mark: she didn’t give it much thought
Emily was directed off the highway
segments.note: 冲突起点：轻视暴风雪，被引下高速

segments.text: 第二段，困境一步步升级：大雪茫茫，几乎没法开车；天黑了，她开始慌，车又滑进了沟里。
mark: The blinding whiteout made driving nearly impossible
panic set in
her car slid into a ditch
segments.note: 困境升级：大雪封路，车滑进沟里

segments.text: 手机没有信号，她只能裹着毯子，在车里过夜。‖情感线很清楚：满怀希望，到慌乱，再到无助。
mark: found no signal on her phone
She wrapped herself in a blanket
segments.note: 情感线：希望 → 慌乱 → 无助

segments.text: 第三段是转机。丹尼尔和瑞秋夫妇在回家路上看到被困的车，停下来帮忙。‖注意这个短语：genuine warmth。真诚的温暖，全文的主题就落在这里：陌生人的善意。
mark: Daniel and his wife Rachel
With genuine warmth in her voice
segments.note: 转机：陌生夫妇停车相助，真诚温暖

segments.text: 艾米丽又感激，又宽慰，接受了帮助。‖情感从无助转向温暖。
mark: Grateful and relieved
segments.note: 情感转折：感激、宽慰

segments.text: 第四段最关键。艾米丽说出了三个难题：离目的地还有一百英里，车完全困住了，整个假期计划可能泡汤。‖续写就要把这三个问题一一解决。
mark: she was about a hundred miles from her destination
her car was completely stuck
her entire holiday plan could be ruined
segments.note: 三个难题：离目的地一百英里；车困住了；假期计划可能泡汤

segments.text: 还有一个细节：夫妇俩给她买了热巧克力，耐心听她说完。‖这份善意，续写的结尾要让艾米丽回报。
mark: the couple bought Emily a hot chocolate and listened patiently
segments.note: 伏笔：热巧克力、耐心倾听——结尾要有回报

segments.text: 再看开头语。第一段开头：夫妇俩建议她坐火车。‖它解决了第一个难题：怎么去多伦多。‖可是车还在沟里，所以这一段必须安排好车，给第二段埋下伏笔。
segments.note: 第一段：解决“怎么去多伦多”，还要安排好那辆车

segments.text: 第二段开头：三天后，她回来取车。‖说明第一段一定交代了车的去处。‖这一段写车怎么样了，写她怎么道谢，最后点明主题。
segments.note: 第二段：回来取车 → 车的结果、道谢回报、点明主题

segments.text: 按这个思路列提纲。第一段四步：讲清方案，附近就有车站；艾米丽担心车，丹尼尔答应拖车保管；夫妇送站，告别落泪；那晚赶到多伦多，赶上圣诞。
lines: ① 讲清方案：附近有车站
② 担心车 → 丹尼尔答应拖车、保管
③ 送站告别，忍不住落泪
④ 那晚到多伦多，赶上圣诞

segments.text: 第二段四步：先写环境，雪停天晴，和暴风雪形成对比；车已经拖出来、清好了雪，兑现承诺；艾米丽送上饼干和卡片，回报善意；最后点题：陌生人的善意，让这个圣诞节成了最温暖的一个。
lines: ① 环境对比：雪停天晴
② 车已拖出、清好雪（兑现承诺）
③ 回报：自制饼干和感谢卡
④ 点题：陌生人让圣诞最温暖

segments.text: 伏笔与呼应。原文说车完全困住了，续写就让丹尼尔找人把车拖出来。
row: have it towed out of the ditch

segments.text: 原文的目标是赶到多伦多见男朋友，续写让她那晚扑进男朋友的怀里。
row: reaching Toronto to meet her boyfriend for Christmas
fell into her boyfriend’s arms in Toronto

segments.text: 原文是茫茫大雪，第二段换成阳光，环境变了，心情也变了。
row: The blinding whiteout made driving nearly impossible

segments.text: 原文担心假期计划泡汤，结尾用同一个词 ruin 收住：差点毁了，却成了最温暖的圣诞。
row: her entire holiday plan could be ruined

segments.text: 原文写瑞秋声音里真诚的温暖，结尾落在最温暖上，主题首尾一贯。‖下面一句一句来写。
row: With genuine warmth in her voice

segments.text: 第一句，先用中文想好：他们解释说，附近就有个火车站，中午有一趟去多伦多的火车。‖为什么要这句？‖开头语只说了坐火车，方案必须落到实处，读者才信。
ln: 为什么：开头语只说“坐火车”，先把方案讲实（车站在哪、几点有车）

segments.text: 汉译英，先定谓语。‖两个分句，两个谓语；插入语 they explained 不算主干。was，一般过去时；would leave，站在过去说将来，用过去将来时。
ln: 谓语：was（一般过去时）；would leave（过去将来时）

segments.text: 再补主语。这是存在句，真正的主语是：a station；后半句的主语：a train to Toronto。
ln: 主语：a station；a train to Toronto

segments.text: 补上 There 和 nearby：附近有个车站。
ln: There 引出存在句；nearby 作地点状语

segments.text: 中间插入一句：they explained，他们解释说。
ln: 插入语：they explained

segments.text: 最后用 and 连起两个分句，句尾补上时间：at noon。
ln: and 连接分句；at noon 交代时间

segments.text: There was a station nearby, they explained, and a train to Toronto would leave at noon.
得分点一，插入语：they explained。‖不写成 they explained that，句式更灵活，对应第三条，语法结构丰富。
segments.src: With genuine warmth in her voice, Rachel said they could take Emily to a nearby cafe they knew.
mark: Rachel said they could take Emily to a nearby cafe
ln: 插入语 they explained：不写 They explained that…，句式更灵活
插入语不算主干，句子主干仍是两个分句

segments.text: 得分点二：a train to Toronto would leave at noon。‖地点、时间都具体，回应原文的一百英里，怎么去的问题解决了，对应第一条，与原文融洽。
segments.hl: a train to Toronto would leave at noon
segments.src: she was about a hundred miles from her destination, her car was completely stuck, and her entire holiday plan could be ruined.
mark: she was about a hundred miles from her destination
ln: 地点、时间都具体：方案可信
解决难题一：离目的地还有一百英里

segments.text: 可替换：The nearest station was just a short drive away。‖后半句也可以写：a train would leave for Toronto at noon。
ln: 可替换：The nearest station was just a short drive away.
可替换：a train would leave for Toronto at noon
替换: The nearest station was just a short drive away.
a train would leave for Toronto at noon

segments.text: 第二句，中文是：可是我的车怎么办？‖艾米丽焦急地问。‖人有办法走了，车还在沟里，这是她的第二个难题，让她自己说出来。
ln: 为什么：人能走了，车还在沟里——让她自己说出第二个难题

segments.text: 谓语：asked，问，一般过去时。
ln: 谓语：asked（一般过去时）

segments.text: 主语：Emily。
ln: 主语：Emily

segments.text: 问的内容用直接引语，放在句首：But what about my car？
ln: 直接引语放句首：“But what about my car?”

segments.text: 最后补一个副词：anxiously，焦急地。
ln: 方式状语：anxiously

segments.text: But what about my car? Emily asked anxiously.
得分点一：直接引语。‖让人物自己开口，比叙述更生动；它接住原文的难题，车完全困住了，又引出下一句丹尼尔的安排，承上启下，对应第一条和第四条。
segments.src: she was about a hundred miles from her destination, her car was completely stuck, and her entire holiday plan could be ruined.
mark: her car was completely stuck
ln: 直接引语：人物开口，比叙述更生动
承上：原文的难题“车困住了”；启下：引出拖车的安排

segments.text: 得分点二：anxiously，一个副词写出焦急。‖原文写过她的慌乱：panic set in；这里的焦急接着这条情感线，后面再转成感激，对应第一条，与原文融洽。
segments.src: As night fell, panic set in.
mark: panic set in
ln: anxiously：一个副词写出焦急
情感线：慌乱 → 焦急，后面再转成感激

segments.text: 可替换：What will happen to my car？‖也可以写：Emily asked with a worried frown。
ln: 可替换：What will happen to my car?
可替换：Emily asked with a worried frown
替换: What will happen to my car?
Emily asked with a worried frown

segments.text: 第三句，中文是：丹尼尔答应找人把车从沟里拖出来，放在他家车库，等她回来。‖它回答了上一句的担心，也给第二段回来取车埋下伏笔。
ln: 为什么：回答“车怎么办”；给第二段“回来取车”埋伏笔

segments.text: 谓语：promised，答应，一般过去时，后面接不定式。
ln: 谓语：promised（一般过去时）+ to do

segments.text: 主语：Daniel。
ln: 主语：Daniel

segments.text: 答应什么？‖to have it towed：have 加宾语，再加过去分词，表示找人把车拖走；车是被拖的，所以用过去分词。
ln: to have it towed：have + 宾语 + 过去分词（找人做）

segments.text: 从哪里拖：out of the ditch。
ln: out of the ditch：从沟里

segments.text: 再并列一个过去分词：and kept in his garage，同样跟在 have it 后面，车被放在车库里。
ln: and kept in his garage：与 towed 并列

segments.text: 最后是时间状语从句：until she returned。‖讲的是过去的承诺，从句用一般过去时表示将来。
ln: until she returned：时间状语从句（一般过去时表将来）

segments.text: Daniel promised to have it towed out of the ditch and kept in his garage until she returned.
得分点一：have it towed，使役结构。‖不是丹尼尔自己去拖，而是找人拖，意思准确，对应第三条。‖它直接回应原文：her car slid into a ditch，车滑进了沟里，ditch 这个词也照应上了。
segments.src: While Emily was driving on a narrow stretch of road, her car slid into a ditch (沟).
mark: her car slid into a ditch
ln: have it towed：使役结构，找人拖，不是自己拖——意思准确
回应原文：车滑进了沟里（ditch）

segments.text: 得分点二：until she returned。‖这是给第二段埋的伏笔。第二段开头说：Three days later, Emily returned to get her car。‖用的是同一个动词 return，两段衔接严丝合缝，对应第一条和第四条。
segments.src: Three days later, Emily returned to get her car.
mark: returned to get her car
ln: 伏笔：until she returned
第二段开头 Emily returned to get her car：同一个动词，衔接严密

segments.text: 可替换：Daniel offered to get the car pulled out，‖后面也可以写：look after it until she came back。
ln: 可替换：Daniel offered to get the car pulled out
可替换：look after it until she came back
替换: Daniel offered to get the car pulled out
look after it until she came back

segments.text: 第四句，中文是：接着，夫妇俩开车送她到车站，陪她一直等到火车进站。‖方案落实了，善意也写足了。
ln: 为什么：方案落地（从咖啡馆到车站），把夫妇的善意写足

segments.text: 谓语有两个：drove，开车送；waited，等。都用一般过去时。
ln: 谓语：drove；waited（并列，一般过去时）

segments.text: 主语：The couple。用 the couple 指两个人，避免反复写名字。
ln: 主语：The couple（指代夫妇俩，不重复名字）

segments.text: drove 后面补上：her to the station，开车送她去车站。
ln: drove her to the station：drive sb to 某地

segments.text: 再补连接成分：then 承接上文，and 连接两个谓语，with her，陪着她。
ln: then 承接；and 连接谓语；with her

segments.text: 最后补时间状语从句：until the train arrived。
ln: until the train arrived：一直等到火车进站

segments.text: The couple then drove her to the station and waited with her until the train arrived.
得分点一：并列谓语，一句两个动作，结构紧凑，对应第三条和第四条。‖原文写这对夫妇，也是这样：注意到被困的车，停下来看能不能帮忙。
segments.hl: drove her to the station and waited with her
segments.src: Standing outside were Daniel and his wife Rachel, who noticed the stranded (被困的) vehicle on their way home and stopped to see if they could help.
mark: noticed the stranded (被困的) vehicle on their way home and stopped
ln: 并列谓语：一句两个动作，结构紧凑
原文写这对夫妇，也是并列谓语：noticed … and stopped

segments.text: 得分点二：waited with her until the train arrived。‖不是送到就走，而是陪着等车，这个细节让善意更具体，对应第二条，内容丰富。‖和原文的耐心倾听一样，写的都是这对夫妇的耐心。
segments.hl: waited with her until the train arrived
segments.src: In the cafe, the couple bought Emily a hot chocolate and listened patiently as she explained her desperate situation
mark: listened patiently
ln: 细节：不是送到就走，而是陪着等车
和原文 listened patiently 一样，写夫妇的耐心

segments.text: 可替换：saw her off at the station，送行；或者：stayed by her side until the train pulled in。
ln: 可替换：saw her off at the station
可替换：stayed by her side until the train pulled in
替换: saw her off at the station
stayed by her side until the train pulled in

segments.text: 第五句，中文是：隔着结霜的车窗向他们挥手，艾米丽几乎忍不住泪水。‖告别是这一段的情感高点，要写出她的感激。
ln: 为什么：告别是情感高点——从无助、焦急到感激

segments.text: 谓语：could hardly hold back。情态动词加 hardly，几乎不能；hold back，忍住。
ln: 谓语：could hardly hold back（几乎忍不住）

segments.text: 主语：Emily。
ln: 主语：Emily

segments.text: 忍住什么：her tears，泪水，作宾语。
ln: 宾语：her tears

segments.text: 句首补上：Waving to them，现在分词作伴随状语。挥手和忍泪同时发生，动作的主语都是 Emily。
ln: Waving to them：现在分词作伴随状语

segments.text: 最后补上地点：through the frosty train window，隔着结了霜的车窗。
ln: through the frosty train window：隔着结霜的车窗

segments.text: Waving to them through the frosty train window, Emily could hardly hold back her tears.
得分点一：现在分词作状语，Waving to them。‖原文就有同样的结构：Seeing no hope of immediate rescue。‖续写模仿原文句式，语言风格统一，对应第三条和第一条。
segments.src: Seeing no hope of immediate rescue, Emily decided to spend the night in her car.
mark: Seeing no hope of immediate rescue
ln: 现在分词作状语：动作和情感同时呈现
原文同样的句式：Seeing no hope of immediate rescue

segments.text: 得分点二：could hardly hold back her tears。‖不直接说她很感激，而是写她忍不住流泪，用动作写情感。‖原文写她 grateful and relieved，这里把感激推到了高点，对应第二条和第一条。
segments.hl: could hardly hold back her tears
segments.src: Grateful and relieved, Emily accepted the offer.
mark: Grateful and relieved
ln: 用动作写情感：不说“很感激”，写她忍不住流泪
情感线：感激、宽慰 → 推到高点

segments.text: 可替换：As the train pulled away，用时间状语从句开头；后面也可以写：Emily felt tears of gratitude welling up in her eyes。
ln: 可替换：As the train pulled away
可替换：Emily felt tears of gratitude welling up in her eyes
替换: As the train pulled away
Emily felt tears of gratitude welling up in her eyes

segments.text: 第六句，中文是：那天晚上，她在多伦多扑进了男朋友的怀里，正好赶上圣诞节。‖第一段收尾，给原文的目标一个结果。
ln: 为什么：第一段收尾——原文的目标（到多伦多和男朋友过圣诞）有了结果

segments.text: 谓语：fell，一般过去时。fall into one’s arms，扑进某人怀里。
ln: 谓语：fell（一般过去时）

segments.text: 主语：she。
ln: 主语：she

segments.text: 补上去向和地点：into her boyfriend’s arms in Toronto。
ln: into her boyfriend’s arms in Toronto

segments.text: 句首补时间：That evening，那天晚上。
ln: 时间状语：That evening

segments.text: 句尾补一句：just in time for Christmas，正好赶上圣诞。
ln: just in time for Christmas：正好赶上

segments.text: That evening, she fell into her boyfriend’s arms in Toronto, just in time for Christmas.
得分点一：fell into her boyfriend’s arms。‖原文开头就说，她满怀希望，要去多伦多见男朋友过圣诞。这里让目标实现，首尾呼应，对应第一条。
segments.src: Emily Sanders, a 25-year-old from Detroit, Michigan, set out on December 23rd with high hopes of reaching Toronto to meet her boyfriend for Christmas.
mark: reaching Toronto to meet her boyfriend for Christmas
ln: 目标实现：到多伦多，见到男朋友
原文开头的 high hopes 有了结果，首尾呼应

segments.text: 得分点二：That evening，时间状语放在句首。‖和第二段开头的 Three days later 连成一条清楚的时间线，对应第四条，连接成分。
segments.src: Three days later, Emily returned to get her car.
mark: Three days later
ln: 时间状语放句首：That evening
与第二段开头 Three days later 连成清楚的时间线

segments.text: 可替换：By nightfall, she had reached Toronto，‖后面也可以写：in time to spend Christmas with her boyfriend。
ln: 可替换：By nightfall, she had reached Toronto
可替换：in time to spend Christmas with her boyfriend

Daniel and Rachel suggested that Emily continue her journey by train. There was a station nearby, they explained, and a train to Toronto would leave at noon. But what about my car? Emily asked anxiously. Daniel promised to have it towed out of the ditch and kept in his garage until she returned. The couple then drove her to the station and waited with her until the train arrived. Waving to them through the frosty train window, Emily could hardly hold back her tears. That evening, she fell into her boyfriend’s arms in Toronto, just in time for Christmas.

Three days later, Emily returned to get her car. The sky was clear now, and the road that had trapped her lay quiet in the sunshine. Parked outside the couple’s garage was her car, cleaned of snow and ready to go. Emily handed them a box of homemade cookies and a card that read, Thank you for saving my holiday. We just did what anyone would do, Rachel said, giving her a warm hug. Driving away, Emily realized that the storm had nearly ruined her Christmas, but two strangers had made it the warmest of her life.

segments.text: 第二，时态混乱。叙事用一般过去时，更早发生的用过去完成时，比如：the road that had trapped her。

segments.text: 第三，lie 和 lay 分不清。路静静地躺着，是 lie 的过去式 lay，不能写成 laid。

segments.text: Daniel and Rachel suggested that Emily continue her journey by train.
There was a station nearby, they explained, and a train to Toronto would leave at noon.
But what about my car? Emily asked anxiously.
Daniel promised to have it towed out of the ditch and kept in his garage until she returned.
The couple then drove her to the station and waited with her until the train arrived.
Waving to them through the frosty train window, Emily could hardly hold back her tears.
That evening, she fell into her boyfriend’s arms in Toronto, just in time for Christmas.
Three days later, Emily returned to get her car.
The sky was clear now, and the road that had trapped her lay quiet in the sunshine.
Parked outside the couple’s garage was her car, cleaned of snow and ready to go.
Emily handed them a box of homemade cookies and a card that read, Thank you for saving my holiday.
We just did what anyone would do, Rachel said, giving her a warm hug.
Driving away, Emily realized that the storm had nearly ruined her Christmas, but two strangers had made it the warmest of her life.
